note: How operators become agents. One invocation of one operator is one agent, created fresh on the operator's own profile (operator.json → resources) with the refs its operator.json declares and nothing else. The orchestrator owns dispatch: it validates the input, starts the agent, validates the output, and follows routing.json to the next operator, user, or external party. It never merges two operators into one agent and never lets an agent start another.

agent.grants: operator.json → resources.requires, and nothing the profile would otherwise permit
agent.refs: operator.json → refs, resolved through refs.json; an unlisted location is unreadable
agent.isolation: fresh, no inherited turns; a critique inside an operator is a step of the same agent
agent.writes: only @artifacts of its own invocation, registered in output.artifactRefs

concurrency.rule: at most maxConcurrentAgents agents at once, and never two agents whose refs share a writable location
concurrency.sharedCheckout: two agents may read one checkout; only one may hold it for writing (backend.implement, fe.source.apply, git.publish are exclusive per checkout)
concurrency.sharedRoot: business.decide is exclusive per businesses root; platform.operate is exclusive per runtime owner

handoff.carrier: the typed receipt under @artifacts; the next agent binds it as @receipt and re-validates
handoff.resume: a blocked receipt with a resume token re-enters the same operator as a new agent
handoff.stop: routing.json kind user or external ends automation; the orchestrator reports and waits
